title: DTM median gridding on measured cells over 0.1 to 10 m cells, origin at the data minimum, against SciPy
question: Over 50 seeded cell sizes from 0.1 to 10 m, on small and UTM-scale coordinates after OLV's LAS ingest, does rasterizeDtm with median aggregation give the same per-cell median as SciPy on the same points and grid, for cells that hold at least one return?

metrics.toleranceUnit: metre (OLV float32 against the reference rounded to float32)

claims.toleranceDerivation: Both sides take the median of the same returns, so the only expected difference is float32 storage on the OLV side. Rounding the reference to float32 removes that, and 1e-6 m then separates a last-bit difference from a different median. Every cell must pass and the occupancy masks must match exactly.

freeze.witness: The commit that adds validation/protocols/dtm-median-gridding-v5.md, which keeps the v4 seed, draws, fixtures, tolerance, edge rule, 600-cell minimum per draw and pass rule, states why v4 failed, and fixes exact reference I/O, before any v5 reference grid existed. The v4 protocol and fixtures were committed before any reference grid at all.

decisionRule: Agree only when every compared cell is within 1e-6 m after rounding the reference to float32, the occupancy masks match exactly, at least 15000 cells are compared, and the two references (SciPy and R terra) agree with each other under the same rule. Otherwise report the failure with its numbers; the tolerance is never widened.
notes: Transcribes validation/protocols/dtm-median-gridding-v5.md (with v4, which it reruns). It does not create that freeze.

Protocol v4 failed on the same draws: the reference grids were written to 9 decimals, which moved even-count medians (float32 ties) off the tie. v5 changes only the reference I/O. The v4 record is kept unchanged.
minimumComparableCells is the total over 50 draws; the protocol also requires at least 600 compared cells in every draw.
